headcount_and_footprint: 840 employees across 90 physical retail stores (flagship city-center and suburban mall locations) plus 1 corporate HQ in Turin
workforce_target: In-Store Sales Associates and Assistant Store Managers (~110 urgent openings ahead of the seasonal peak)
organizational_context: Mid-sized national fashion and lifestyle retailer expanding mall locations. Declared EVP on our careers site: 'A vibrant, people-first fashion community where creativity and work-life balance thrive.'

ingaze_platform_signals.reputation_and_reviews: Overall public rating sits at 3.4/5 across Glassdoor and Indeed, but it hides a huge split: HQ reviews average 4.2/5 while suburban mall stores sit at 2.9/5. Recent store-staff reviews repeatedly complain about unpredictable last-minute weekend shift changes, burnout during holiday peaks, and store managers who never give feedback or scheduling notice. Note: our raw review export also accidentally pulled 2 unverified rows from an external third-party warehouse pilot complaining about 'overnight forklift charging bays'.
ingaze_platform_signals.recruiting_and_jds: Our career page gets solid smartphone traffic (~79% mobile visitors), mostly young retail candidates browsing during commutes, yet 61% abandon the application halfway through. The portal still forces candidates to create a desktop account, verify email, and upload a formatted PDF resume across 5 screens. Store job ads are copy-pasted from old HQ templates ('synergistic brand ambassador with omnichannel KPI mindset') and never mention shift rules or store perks.
ingaze_platform_signals.linkedin_and_content_analytics: Our corporate LinkedIn page gets decent engagement from fashion buyers and HQ marketers, but almost zero applications for in-store roles. Meanwhile, our 2-person HR ops team spends roughly 12 hours every month manually copying store Google/Indeed reviews into an Excel tracker.

client_internal_context.healthy_metrics_and_strengths_not_to_bre: Base hourly pay for sales associates is actually 10% above the regional retail average (exit interviews almost never cite base pay), employees love the 40% staff product discount, and our Turin HQ design/merchandising teams maintain 92% annual retention.
client_internal_context.cohort_and_site_asymmetries: HQ and our 12 city-center flagship stores hire smoothly and keep staff long-term. The real bleeding is concentrated in the 78 suburban mall stores, where 24% of newly hired sales associates quit within their first 6 months due to chaotic weekend rosters and newly promoted store managers with zero people-management training.
client_internal_context.budget_and_capacity_constraints: Store turnover and emergency weekend temp coverage are costing us an estimated €420k/year in replacement and lost-sales drag. The CFO has put a freeze on extra job-board ad spend until HR can show hard numbers on turnover risk and conversion ROI instead of social media likes.
client_internal_context.leadership_perceptions_and_requests: The VP of Retail wants to immediately launch an Employee Ambassador campaign on Instagram and TikTok next month asking mall store staff to film 'Day in the Life' videos to fix our applicant shortage. At the same time, the Head of Marketing suggested a weekly B2B LinkedIn thought-leadership blog series to attract store associates, and Finance asked if we should cut the 40% staff discount to fund recruiting ads.

hr_intake_notes: Honestly, we feel stuck in a loop. Mall store managers keep calling HQ asking for more candidates, we burn hours tracking reviews in spreadsheets, and the people we do manage to hire in the malls leave after a few rough weekends. Leadership wants quick visibility campaigns before next quarter, but we're worried we're fixing the wrong things.
